correctness.rationale: The geometric matrix power identity H_t^j=H_{t^j} is verified from Möbius composition. H_t is the dual of A_t on H^1 and of B_t=J A_t J^-1 on Bergman A^1; direct change-of-variables and Hardy subordination give ||H_{t^j}||<=Ct^{-j}. Independent predual functions (1-z)^s with t^s=w for all imaginary branches yield an infinite-dimensional annihilator of each punctured-disk range. Analytic conjugation v=z/(1-z) reduces any point eigenvector to a boundary pole z^k/(1-z)^{k+1}, not a Bloch function; BMOA embeds into Bloch. Spectral mapping in the operator and Calkin algebras then gives both spectral identities for F(H_t). Holomorphic factorization proves injectivity of F(H_t)-lambda, and predual eigenvectors give the infinite-codimension claims. Boundaries and the case of infinitely many atoms are included via analytic-radius and norm convergence. Exact-rational coefficient checker independently passed 21360 finite assertions, without purporting to establish infinite-dimensional claims.

originality.rationale: The relevant 2026 BMOA/Bloch paper requires Mellin membership in the extended Dunford–Riesz class; the geometric-lattice Mellin transform is nonconstant imaginary-periodic and violates its limit-at-infinity requirement. The prior 2006 BMOA/Bloch Hausdorff paper addresses boundedness, not the present exact spectrum. The 2024 generalized Hausdorff paper treats a family of other holomorphic spaces, based on accessible abstract; inaccessible complete text is an explicit historical-priority risk. Searches for geometric atomic measures, equivalent dilation/composition formulations, ordinary and Calkin spectra, and no-point-spectrum variants returned no covering claim. No claim of proof of novelty from search alone.

Other equivalent spectral-calculus or Hausdorff-matrix results not returned by the available queries could predate this finding.
The sharp analytic-radius boundary rho=t^-1 is not addressed.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 spectral theorem leaves a natural, highly singular atomic Mellin class uncovered. The complete spectrum, Fredholm essential spectrum, point-spectrum absence, and infinite-dimensional residual obstruction are all determined explicitly on both BMOA and Bloch for a countably infinite family of nonconstant positive analytic generating functions. An exact infinite-codimension Fredholm-collapse characterization is a structural classification rather than a routine bound, isolated counterexample or known-table recalculation.
